## Improved - Several swipes in a row are smoother. After each swipe Butterfly brought the next app forward on the same thread that draws the motion, so the next swipe could stutter. - The strip map no longer makes a move stutter when a window crosses the edge of the screen. - Opening or closing a window, or starting an app, while the strip is moving no longer interrupts the move. The strip picks up the change as soon as it stops.
## Fixed - A window you bring back from the Dock now appears right where it stays. Before, it showed up at its old place for a moment and then moved. - A window that goes full screen on a second display keeps its place on the strip. Before, it could come back as a new window at half the width of the screen.

## New - Workspace templates: pick Code, Work, Research, Meeting or Home from the ⛓ menu or Settings and Butterfly makes a new workspace with the right apps side by side, and where it helps, one above the other (Claude over Terminal, chat over mail). Apps that are closed open in the background. - Each template suggests apps you already have on your Mac. Swap any of them, choose none, or put any other app in a slot before you create the workspace. - New windows of a template's apps go to its workspace, so a new Slack or Mail window lands where you work with it. A short capsule shows where it went. You can turn this off per template. - Save the current workspace as your own template, and apply any template to the workspace you are in. - Butterfly can learn which apps you use together, only on your Mac and without window titles, and suggests a template made from your usage. You can turn this off or clear the data in Settings. - The tour ends with a step to start with a template. - When you create a workspace from a template, show the desktop or bring windows back, each window turns into a butterfly made of its app icon that flies to its place and turns back into the window.
## Improved - Workspaces, templates and saved layouts live together in Settings › Workspaces & Layouts. The current workspace shows its apps and a small picture of its layout, and every template shows its layout before you create it. - A new workspace from a template fits your screen, so all its windows are visible right away. - Settings buttons never wrap, and the Settings window is a little larger. - When you drag the edge of a window to change its width, the column now keeps that width, like after ⌃⌥R. It stays after you move along the strip and after Butterfly restarts. When you drag a window's left edge to the left, the edge stays where you let go and the strip moves under it.
## Fixed - Restoring a saved layout while its windows are open now moves the windows into place right away. - Showing an app that was hidden no longer moves its windows to another workspace. - The thin strip of a window parked at the edge of the screen, and the corner of a window from a hidden workspace, no longer react to clicks. Before, a click right at the screen edge could bring a hidden window forward.

## New - Double-click a window's title bar to make it full width, and again to bring its width back. It works like ⌃⌥F and follows your macOS setting for double-clicking a title bar (Fill).
## Improved - Butterfly fits the strip to each screen on its own. On smaller screens the gaps are tighter, a new window fills almost the whole screen with the next window peeking in at the side, and ⌃⌥R skips widths that would make a window too narrow to use. On very wide screens, three new windows fit side by side. - On windows too narrow for all tab icons, the tab capsule folds into the active tab's icon and the number of tabs. Point at it to unfold it. - The window map is smaller on screens with less height. - In the Full Butterfly theme, windows you are not working in no longer show old content while the strip moves. Butterfly checks them every few seconds with a tiny preview and takes a fresh shot only when something changed, so it stays as light as before.
## Fixed - A window that can't get narrower than its column, such as Photos at half the width of a smaller screen, no longer covers the window next to it. Its column now takes the window's own width. - Switching a tab to a window of another app, with a click on the tab capsule or a shortcut, now brings that app to the front and you can type in it right away. Before, only the icon changed. - Moving the focus with the keyboard, or swiping to some apps (such as Dia), now brings that app to the front too.
